title: Drishyam 3 at Rs 540.79 Crore Worldwide, Within Rs 20 Crore of Padmaavat
excerpt: After 16 days, Ajay Devgn's Drishyam: The Conclusion stands Rs 19.21 crore short of Padmaavat's Rs 560 crore lifetime total, with Sanju's No. 21 spot set to fall first.
body:
• Drishyam 3 has grossed Rs 540.79 crore worldwide in 16 days, according to Koimoi - Rs 403.10 crore gross in India and Rs 137.69 crore overseas.
  • That leaves it Rs 19.21 crore short of Padmaavat's Rs 560 crore lifetime total, the highest-grossing film of Sanjay Leela Bhansali's career.
  • At No. 22 on the all-time Bollywood worldwide list, the Ajay Devgn film must first pass Sanju at Rs 541.76 crore before it can take Padmaavat's No. 20 spot.
  • Made on a reported budget of Rs 110 crore, the film has already returned a 206% profit on Koimoi's calculation.

Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3, released as Drishyam: The Conclusion, has grossed Rs 540.79 crore worldwide after 16 days in cinemas, putting it within Rs 20 crore of the lifetime total of Padmaavat, the highest-grossing film directed by Sanjay Leela Bhansali.

According to Koimoi, the suspense thriller directed by Abhishek Pathak has collected Rs 403.10 crore gross in India, on a net collection of Rs 341.6 crore, and Rs 137.69 crore overseas. It is now closing on the Rs 550 crore mark in its third week.

The records in its path

Padmaavat, starring Deepika Padukone and Ranveer Singh, holds a lifetime worldwide collection of Rs 560 crore and the No. 20 spot on the all-time highest-grossing Bollywood films worldwide list, Koimoi reported. Drishyam 3 stands at No. 22, Rs 19.21 crore behind Padmaavat. Between the two sits Ranbir Kapoor's Sanju at No. 21, with a lifetime collection of Rs 541.76 crore - less than Rs 1 crore ahead of Drishyam 3's current total, and the first record set to fall.

The economics are already settled, whatever happens next. Koimoi put the film's budget at Rs 110 crore, its profit at Rs 226.6 crore and its return on investment at 206%.

How it got here

The run has been front-loaded but durable. Reporting by IWMBuzz, citing Sacnilk, put the film at Rs 328.75 crore net in India and Rs 509 crore worldwide after 13 days, with an overseas gross of Rs 115 crore at that point. Its opening day brought Rs 62 crore net in India, followed by Rs 53.50 crore and Rs 61 crore over its first weekend, before weekday collections settled into single digits in the second week - Rs 5.25 crore net on day 13 across 14,717 shows.

The three days between the two reports added more than Rs 30 crore worldwide, driven substantially overseas, where the gross rose from Rs 115 crore to Rs 137.69 crore. That overseas strength matters for the final ranking: diaspora audiences in North America, the United Kingdom and the Gulf have carried the film past the point where domestic collections alone would have stalled.

What it means

Passing Padmaavat would be a striking result for a thriller franchise with no spectacle-driven set pieces of the kind Bhansali's film was built on. Drishyam 3's cast - Devgn alongside Tabu, Shriya Saran and Jaideep Ahlawat, in a film produced by Kumar Mangat Pathak, Abhishek Pathak and Ajit Andhare under Panorama Studios, Viacom18 Studios and Star Studios - sold a conclusion audiences had waited for since Drishyam 2, and the numbers show that familiarity, rather than scale, did the work.

What to watch

The remaining gap to Padmaavat is Rs 19.21 crore gross. At the pace implied by the day-13 to day-16 reports, the film should pass Sanju within days and then test Padmaavat before its run ends - provided third-weekend collections in overseas markets hold. Box-office trackers will update the worldwide total daily; the No. 20 spot is now a question of when, not whether the chase continues.
